findings.claim: For complex obs saved before 2.8 (bare filename relative to the obs dir, i.e. every existing complex obs on an upgraded install) a read still costs 6 filesystem operations exactly as on master, 3 of them Files.exists plus a failed stat, so TRUNK-6682's 'at most one existence-related check' criterion is met only for new-layout keys, and the PR description's '5 -> 3' figure describes only that case; does the ticket stay open for the legacy half (dkayiwa's unanswered question in thread r4070873940)?
findings.evidence: Wrote a throwaway BaseContextSensitiveTest (deleted) that wraps java.nio.file.Files in Mockito.mockStatic(CALLS_REAL_METHODS) and logs exists/readAttributes/newInputStream under the app data dir during AbstractHandler.getObs and TextHandler.getObs(TEXT_VIEW). GP obs.complex_obs_dir=complex_obs. PR head 86b96c7d6: new-layout key = 3 ops (exists=true, readAttributes, newInputStream), matching the PR's claim (known-good control); 2.7-era obs (valueComplex 'title|<name>', file at appData/complex_obs/<name>) = 6 ops: exists=false storage/<name>, exists=false appData/<name> (parseDataKey -> LocalStorageService.exists:279-293), readAttributes FAILED NoSuchFileException storage/complex_obs/<name> then exists=true appData/complex_obs/<name> (LocalStorageService.read:99-112), readAttributes, newInputStream. Same probe on master (git switch --detach master): new layout 6 ops (4 exists), 2.7-era legacy 6 ops (4 exists). So new layout 6->3, legacy 6->6. All handler counting tests (AbstractHandlerTest/BinaryData/BinaryStream/Image/Media/TextHandlerTest getObs_shouldReadDataAndMetadataInASingleStorageCall) save via saveObs, i.e. only new-layout keys; none pins the legacy count. Ticket TRUNK-6682 acceptance criterion 1 and description ('resolve the legacy-vs-new key layout without a separate existence probe where possible (or cache the resolution)').

findings.claim: TRUNK-6682 carries the `backport` label and StorageService itself is '@since 2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15', but the new API is '@since 3.0.0' only and the handler/storage code uses Java 16+ constructs (private record ImageHandler.LoadedImage at ImageHandler.java:153, pattern-matching instanceof at S3StorageService.java:178) that the maintenance lines, built with javaCompilerVersion 1.8, cannot compile; is this master-only, or should it be written so it can be cherry-picked and @since list the maintenance versions?
findings.evidence: Ticket JSON labels: backport, community-priority, performance. `git show a085b50b6^:pom.xml` (last commit before 'Bump version to 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT', i.e. where 2.8.x branched) has <javaCompilerVersion>1.8</javaCompilerVersion> feeding maven-compiler-plugin source/target; master pom has maven.compiler.release 21 (dcf1695d6). grep @since in StorageService.java: class '2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15', new method '3.0.0'; DataWithMetadata.java:21 '@since 3.0.0'. ibacher's thread r3990860896 ('We can't backport this implementation') and dkayiwa's r4070873955 asked for the backport versions; the head answers with 3.0.0 only. S3StorageService was added after the 3.0.0 bump (658a3df03), so its line matters only if it was backported.

verdict: Close to mergeable for master: the new-layout read drops from 6 to 3 filesystem ops with call-count tests that go red on regression. What's left is a scope decision: legacy-layout obs are not improved at all (6 -> 6 ops), and the ticket's backport label clashes with Java 16+ code and @since 3.0.0.
